title: Sika FastFix vs Gator Maxx vs Techniseal RG+: Polymeric Sand
h1: Sika FastFix vs Gator Maxx vs Techniseal RG+
query: sika fastfix vs gator maxx vs techniseal
keywords: techniseal rg+ vs gator maxx g2
description: Gator Maxx G2 fills 1/8 to 4 inch joints and is rain-safe 15 minutes after watering; Techniseal RG+ stops at 1 inch; Sika FastFix-110 needs 24 h to walk on.
dek: Three bags that look alike but differ on joint width, rain tolerance and drying rules.
quickAnswer: For most patios, walkways and driveways, Gator Maxx G2 is the most flexible choice: it fills joints from 1/8 to 4 inches, is rain-safe 15 minutes after watering, installs above 32°F and carries a 15-year residential limited warranty. Techniseal RG+ suits narrow-to-medium joints up to 1 inch and resists surprise rain 90 minutes after installation. Sika FastFix-110 covers 1/8 to 4 inches but asks for 24 hours dry before foot traffic and 72 before vehicles.
intro: Polymeric sand looks like a commodity, a 50-pound bag of fine sand with a binder in it, and Alliance Gator, Techniseal and Sika sit side by side at the same stores. The bags are not interchangeable: they are rated for different joint widths, tolerate rain at very different points after watering, and have different temperature and drying rules. Picking the wrong one for your joints is one of the most common reasons a paver job washes out or hazes over.

This comparison covers Alliance Gator Maxx G2, Techniseal RG+ and Sika FastFix-110. The figures come from each maker's published technical data sheets and product pages; we have not installed these sands ourselves, and where a figure could not be confirmed we say so. Formulas change, so check the bag and the current data sheet. For a wider field, see our [best polymeric sand](/best-polymeric-sand/) rankings.

sections.h: Which Is the Best Polymeric Sand: Sika FastFix, Gator Maxx or Techniseal?

blocks.p: There is no single best polymeric sand; there is a best sand for your joints and your weather. Three questions decide it.

If any joint is wider than 1 inch, as with flagstone, bluestone or tumbled pavers with irregular edges, Techniseal RG+ is outside its rated range and Gator Maxx G2 or Sika FastFix-110 (both up to 4 inches) are the candidates. For standard concrete pavers with tight 1/8- to 3/8-inch joints, all three work.

blocks.h3: How sure are you of the weather?

blocks.p: Gator Maxx G2 is rated rain-safe 15 minutes after water activation in traditional installs. Techniseal RG+ says it can resist an unforeseen rain 90 minutes after installation but recommends planning for 24 hours without rain. Sika FastFix-110 claims a fast gel time to resist unexpected rain and asks you to protect the surface from rain while it dries for at least 24 hours.

Gator Maxx G2 can be installed above 32°F in dry conditions. Sika FastFix-110 lists a 40-95°F range for both air and surface. Techniseal RG+ says the temperature should stay above 32°F (0°C) through its 48-hour drying period.

sections.h: Which Sika FastFix Is It? Two Different Products

blocks.p: Search for Sika FastFix and you will find two different things.

Sika FastFix-110 is a polymeric sand sold in North America. Sika's product data sheet describes it as a high-performance polymeric sand for joints between interlocking pavers, stone, bricks and slabs, applied dry, compacted with a plate compactor and activated with water, the same method as Gator and Techniseal. It is the one compared on this page.

Sika FastFix All Weather is a ready-mixed, brush-in jointing compound sold mainly in the UK and Ireland. It is not sand you water in: Sika's literature says it can be applied in any weather, even in rain, and tells you not to add extra sand. Its published minimums are a 5 mm joint width and 20 mm depth, and in dry weather above about 15°C setting starts in 6 to 12 hours. It belongs to a different category and is not a like-for-like alternative to North American polymeric sand.
If you are in the US or Canada and the bag says polymeric sand, you are looking at FastFix-110 or a similar product.

sections.h: Which Polymeric Sand Handles the Widest Joints?

blocks.p: Gator Maxx G2 and Sika FastFix-110 tie at 4 inches; Techniseal RG+ stops at 1 inch. Every polymeric sand is designed for a range of joint widths, and using it outside that range is the most common cause of failure. Joints too narrow for the sand do not fill to full depth; joints too wide do not bind strongly and crack or wash out.

Techniseal RG+ is rated from 1/16 inch (1.5 mm) to 1 inch (2.5 cm), with a 1-1/2 inch minimum depth. Its data sheet also tells you when to choose something else: for high-humidity areas, false joints, joints wider than 4 inches, heavy traffic such as large commercial lots, steep slopes or standing water, Techniseal recommends its HP2 high-performance sand instead.

Gator Maxx G2 is rated from 1/8 inch to 4 inches in traditional installs, and up to 2 inches for overlays (pavers laid over an existing concrete slab), with a 1-1/2 inch minimum depth. Alliance lists it for concrete, natural stone, wet-cast and clay pavers on patios, walkways, pool decks, driveways, parking areas and steep slopes. Driveways need fully interlocked pavers.

Sika FastFix-110 is rated from 3 mm to 100 mm (1/8 to 4 inches) for joints between interlocking pavers, stone, bricks and slabs, including walkways, patios, driveways, pool surrounds, parking areas and light-traffic roadways.

Measure your widest joints before buying. For natural stone, where joints often run from narrow to well over an inch, a 1/8-to-4-inch product is the safer choice. Our guide to [polymeric sand vs regular sand](/polymeric-sand-vs-regular-sand-for-pavers/) covers when a plain jointing sand is the better call.

sections.h: Which One Is Safest If It Rains, and How Long Does Each Take to Cure?

blocks.p: Rain is the biggest risk in any polymeric sand job. Water activates the binder; too much water too soon washes the binder out of the joint or onto the paver faces, where it dries as haze. Our guide to [how to use polymeric sand](/how-to-use-polymeric-sand/) covers the watering technique; the three products differ mainly in how quickly they stop being vulnerable.

ul: Gator Maxx G2: rain-safe 15 minutes after water activation in traditional installs (24 hours for overlays), credited to what Alliance calls Rapid Set technology. Installs above 32°F in dry conditions.

Techniseal RG+: starts to set a few minutes after wetting and becomes water-resistant 90 minutes after installation. Techniseal still recommends planning for 24 hours without rain and above 0°C (32°F) through the 48-hour drying period. The surface must be dry before you spread the sand, or the polymer activates early and sticks to the pavers.

Sika FastFix-110: claims a fast gel time to resist unexpected rain, lists 40-95°F for air and surface, and says to let the surface dry at least 24 hours, protected from rain, before foot traffic and 72 hours before vehicles.

blocks.p: Whatever you choose, read the forecast for the whole drying period, not just the first hour. A downpour on uncured sand is the most common reason people end up searching for [how to remove polymeric sand haze](/how-to-remove-polymeric-sand-haze-from-pavers/).

sections.h: Which One Leaves the Least Haze and Is Easiest to Install?

blocks.p: Gator Maxx G2 is marketed on ease: no dust, haze free, no blower, one watering. Alliance says its polymers neutralize haze and dust, and that the sand is ASTM C144 graded to fit tight joints. For a first-time installer worried about haze that is a meaningful claim, though good practice (sweep off residue, water gently) still applies.

Techniseal RG+ takes the traditional route: spread on a dry surface, sweep into the joints, compact with a plate compactor (with a rubber mat on textured pavers), repeat until joints are packed to the bottom of the chamfer or at least 1/8 inch below the top, and remove all residue before wetting. Techniseal says that without mechanical compaction the joints remain weak and fail quickly.

Sika FastFix-110 follows a similar method: sweep in, compact in different directions, repeat, level with a leaf blower and blow off the excess, soak sections of about 50 square feet for roughly 60 seconds from about 3 feet away starting at the bottom of any slope, then blow excess water off the surface. Sika says that second blowing step is needed to remove residue.
None of these is difficult, but each method is slightly different and the warranty usually depends on following it. Use the instructions for the bag you bought, not a generic video.

sections.h: Why Do Polymeric Sands Cost Different Amounts, and What Are the Warranties?

blocks.p: Within these three, a higher price usually buys a wider joint range, faster rain resistance, easier haze-free installation or a longer warranty, not stronger joints in a simple sense. A sand rated for 4-inch joints uses a binder system designed to hold a wide, deep joint together; a sand rated to 1 inch can be simpler.

Alliance offers a 15-year limited warranty on Gator Maxx G2 for residential projects (1 year for commercial and institutional work). The remedy is a refund of the purchase price, proof of purchase is required, installation must follow Alliance's specifications and industry standards, and moss, mold and mildew are excluded. We did not find comparable published residential warranty terms for Techniseal RG+ or Sika FastFix-110 on the sheets we read, so check their current terms. Any warranty typically covers the material, not your labor.
Still deciding whether polymeric sand is right at all? See [polymeric sand pros and cons](/polymeric-sand-pros-and-cons/).

blocks.p: Planning to seal the pavers too? Let the sand cure fully first; our [paver sealer](/best-paver-sealer/) guide covers the timing and products.

mistakes: Techniseal RG+ is rated to 1 inch. Bluestone and flagstone joints often run wider, and sand outside its range cracks or washes out. Measure the widest joint first and choose a 1/8-to-4-inch sand such as Gator Maxx G2 or FastFix-110.

Polymeric binder starts working the moment it gets wet. Sand swept over a damp surface sticks to the paver faces and dries as haze. Techniseal says the surface must be dry before spreading; wait for a dry day and a dry slab.
Techniseal says joints that are not mechanically compacted remain weak and fail quickly, and Sika's directions compact twice. Sweeping alone leaves voids that settle, crack and let weeds back in.
Mixing up the two Sika products

Sika FastFix All Weather is a UK brush-in jointing compound that can go down in rain; Sika FastFix-110 is a North American polymeric sand you sweep, compact and water. Following the wrong instructions ruins either one.
bottomLine: Match the sand to your joints first, then to your weather. Gator Maxx G2 is the best fit for most projects because it covers 1/8 to 4 inch joints, is rain-safe 15 minutes after watering, installs above 32°F and carries a 15-year residential limited warranty. Techniseal RG+ is a sound, often cheaper choice for tight concrete paver joints up to 1 inch. Sika FastFix-110 matches Gator's joint range but needs a dry day plus 24 hours before foot traffic and 72 before cars. Whichever you buy, spread dry, compact twice and water gently.

faqs.q: Which is the best polymeric sand: Sika FastFix, Gator Maxx or Techniseal RG+?
faqs.a: For most projects, Gator Maxx G2, because it covers joints from 1/8 to 4 inches, is rain-safe 15 minutes after watering and installs above 32°F. Techniseal RG+ is a good choice for joints up to 1 inch. Sika FastFix-110 matches Gator's joint range but needs 24 hours dry before foot traffic and 72 before vehicles.

faqs.q: What is the difference between polymeric sand brands at different price points?
faqs.a: Mostly joint range, rain tolerance, ease of installation and warranty. Premium sands tend to handle wider joints, resist rain sooner after watering and claim haze-free installation; cheaper sands may be limited to narrower joints and need longer dry windows. Match the sand to your joint width first, then to your weather.

faqs.q: Is Sika FastFix All Weather the same as polymeric sand?
faqs.a: No. Sika FastFix All Weather, sold mainly in the UK and Ireland, is a ready-mixed jointing compound you brush in, and Sika says it can be applied even in rain. Sika FastFix-110, sold in North America, is a polymeric sand you sweep in, compact and water.

faqs.q: Which polymeric sand is best for bluestone?
faqs.a: Bluestone joints are often wider and more irregular than concrete paver joints, so choose a sand rated for wide joints: Gator Maxx G2 or Sika FastFix-110, both up to 4 inches. Check the minimum depth (1-1/2 inches for Gator) and test a small area for color and haze first.

faqs.q: How long does polymeric sand take to cure?
faqs.a: It varies by product. Gator Maxx G2 is rain-safe 15 minutes after activation; Techniseal RG+ resists rain after 90 minutes and has a 48-hour drying period; Sika FastFix-110 needs 24 hours before foot traffic and 72 before vehicles. Cool, humid weather lengthens all of them.

faqs.q: Is there a new type of polymeric sand on the market?
faqs.a: Makers update formulas regularly; Alliance's G2 generation and Techniseal's NextGel line are examples. The main improvements are faster rain resistance, lower dust and haze, and wider joint ranges. Resin-type jointing compounds such as Sika FastFix All Weather are a separate category, more common in Europe.

faqs.q: How many bags of polymeric sand do I need?
faqs.a: It depends on joint width and paver size. Alliance lists 65 to 85 square feet per 50 lb bag of Gator Maxx G2 for narrow joints and 22 to 42 for wide joints on pavers 2-3/8 inches tall; Sika lists 60 to 90 and 20 to 40 square feet for FastFix-110. Buy an extra bag for irregular stone.
